![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/efe8084c2e5b9d5eff4f75dffc9acce77aa66ab0dc62c699589573d96f884d49.png)

The region above enclosed by the curves $y={x}^{2}-2$ and $y=-{x}^{2}$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=-2.$ Find the volume of the resulting solid.
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2 & =-{x}^{2} \\ 2{x}^{2} & =2 \\ {x}^{2} & =1 \\ x & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, our limits of integration are from $x=-1$ to $x=1.$

Now, let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/4514019be21deb238c92f557cc041aec9b5e6629bc9d7dcac133a7aa2aed89c7.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $y={x}^{2}-2,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $y=-{x}^{2}.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $y=-{x}^{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/611d10f83c76467c69a1510809738611962dd5d1e1c22a10b0cb3081d2aa52cc.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}[\,(-{x}^{2})-(-2)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}{[2-{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $y={x}^{2}-2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/683244c0b5be598da85a8875708f459d4f87319677111f1072c997d911075d68.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}[\,(\text{upper})-(\text{lower})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}[\,({x}^{2}-2)-(-2)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}{[{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}{[2-{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x-\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}{[{x}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}((2-{x}^{2})^{2}-({x}^{2})^{2})\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}(4-4{x}^{2}+{x}^{4}-{x}^{4})\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}(4-4{x}^{2})\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {(4x-\frac{4{x}^{3}}{3})|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\pi ((4(1)-\frac{4(1)^{3}}{3})-(4(-1)-\frac{4(-1)^{3}}{3})) \\  & =\pi ((4-\frac{4}{3})-(-4+\frac{4}{3})) \\  & =\pi (8-\frac{8}{3}) \\  & =\frac{16\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
